mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE dropped by more than 0.3pp within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained increases in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k in 1 month and UNRATE drop > 0.2pp
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200k and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% within a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, indicates strong consumer demand and a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month and UNRATE drop > 0.2pp
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% within two months and GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% in the same period, it signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 1% and GDPC1 growth > 2% in 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% and GDPC1 grew by more than 2% within two months.
